newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Heavy rains lash northern Colombia, 12 dead.
newsitem.headline: Heavy rains lash northern Colombia, 12 dead.

text.p: At least 12 people have died in torrential rains across northern Colombia since the weekend and weathermen said on Tuesday that no early relief was in sight.

Hundreds have been left homeless after heavy rains lashed Santander and Norte de Santander provinces. Authorities said a young boy, who died on Monday night when a landslide destroyed his home in Bucaramanga city, was among the latest fatalities.
Ten other people died in flash floods and landslides over the weekend, and civil defence officials said one person was missing and presumed dead.

Miriam Neiva, of the Colombian Civil Defence, said: "Our local committees are on alert in the entire country, carrying out prevention work and warning residents in areas at risk, particularly those alongside rivers. We are helping evacuate people and taking in vital supplies to affected areas."
A National Meteorology Service spokeswoman said that the rainy season, which started a little later than usual this month, would last until mid-November.
"A series of factors mean the rains will be a little heavier this year than last. That is likely to cause rivers to rise to higher than normal levels and could cause landslides," she said.
